challenge.better_approach: Leave the site alone and let spanning ticket B's scan tolerate it: that keeps N doors, which the ruling forbids. A bus verb: this site must answer with no bus. So the published tool, lazily imported, is the smallest move.
challenge.hidden_assumption: poke_target used the raw nodename while superclaude lowercases and shortens it; on a box whose nodename has capitals or a domain the two differed, and the change fixes that rather than breaking it. Measured on akiendelllinux only (nodename already short and lowercase).

answers.falsifier: Done when: an AST scan of cairn/devices/cc/shim.py, cairn/devices/cc/scripts/memory_sync.py, cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_an_idle_cc_session_is_told_it_has_mail.py, cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_a_launch_moves_off_a_held_instance.py, cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_superclaude_sets_cairn_user.py finds no call to os.uname, platform.node, platform.uname or socket.gethostname, and every host name those files read comes from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host.host_name AND with os.uname deleted from the os module for the call, CCShim.poke_target() returns host_name() + '_cc_0', the spelling superclaude gives the session (cairn/devices/cc/superclaude:260 lowercases the short hostname, :290 appends _cc_<instance>). Wrong intent if the system device's tool cannot answer here (an import cycle, or a caller that must run before cairn is on sys.path).
answers.from_idea: none, because it is a child of spanning ticket a577fd03e307, whose measured sites were grepped over cairn/devices/system_rackmount/rackmount.py's neighbours on 2026-11-21 and whose ruling is outline 6.6.3.7 in cairn/devices/cairn/requirements/06-recovery-device.md
answers.how: shim.py:100 becomes a lazy `from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host import host_name` inside poke_target. memory_sync.py runs by absolute path with no PYTHONPATH, so import host_name after its existing sys.path insert (memory_sync.py:52), and on ImportError fall back to naming no host in the commit message rather than failing the Stop hook. The three proofs bind their host from host_name() in place of the hand spelling, and test_an_idle_cc_session_is_told_it_has_mail.py:106 compares poke_target() to f"{host_name()}_cc_0". This is a proof edit: the intention those proofs show PROVED is unchanged, only where they read the name from.
answers.traces_to: Outline 6.6.3.7 (the hostname comes from the system device); outline 2.3.7.1.5 (the system device's host tool is one of the client tools a device publishes, the named exception to 2.3.7; a CC by-line builds, 0.4.1); outline 17.26.1 (a published client tool lives with its device); RULE 1 (the system device's public interface is the tool it publishes); Law 1 (one answer, not N re-derivations of it).
answers.what: The cc device names its host through the system device's host tool: cairn/devices/cc/shim.py:100; cairn/devices/cc/scripts/memory_sync.py:48; cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_an_idle_cc_session_is_told_it_has_mail.py:106; cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_a_launch_moves_off_a_held_instance.py:48; cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_superclaude_sets_cairn_user.py:116 read the host from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host and nowhere else, so this component names its box on every OS.
